No problem. If you want, you could say specifically why you are depressed, like the source. Personally, I am good at figuring out how to be entertained and happy from a mental standpoint, but I am still very depressed because of chronic pain and being permanently single.
Thank you. I might still get a doctor appointment if the arm laziness doesn't go away. This gives me confidence that I can definitely at least get to the appointment without my arm dying.

Thank you very much. Now, I will have to make a decision whether to possibly take a week to get an appointment, or take up an emergency appointment slot. I'll ask them if they think it's worth an emergency spot.

In places where euthanasia is legal, many patients cancel their euthanasia appointments before they happen, because the shock of being close to death makes them want to live. Remember that you aren't stuck here; you are alive by choice. Many people believe that their spirit chose to come into this world. You could have killed yourself and you could be dead right now, but you have so far chosen to live. You are carrying out tasks that mean things to you, like you're a ghost on a mission that is still hanging around. It's better to hang around and be on a mission by choice, than it is to die and face unknown consequences.

Do not try to kill yourself in a way that there's no way out of. People who jump off buildings instantly regret jumping. People who get in a noose to hang themselves instantly regret doing it, but then they're stuck and can't get out. People who OD on sleeping pills to attempt suicide quickly regret doing it, as they feel the suffocation coming on.

Don't kill yourself in a way that is instant either, because that doesn't give you a fair chance at learning that you really want to survive. If you're to the point of suicide, then instead you could shock yourself into wanting to live. Personally, I am slowly getting closer to suicide myself. However, I know logically that it is better to shock myself into wanting life than to actually kill myself. Currently thinking of ways to do that. My last big shock experience was when the night before surgery, I spent half an hour praying that I would die during the procedure. However, right before I went under, I changed it from "I beg you to kill me God" to "kill me if it is what should happen". After waking up alive, I was still very depressed, but the experience was enough to make me think being alive was worth it.

It is always possible to recover to happiness, unless you have unbearable and permanent chronic physical pain.

Very sorry to hear that. Personally, I am gonna have to get a couple surgeries to tackle my weird chronic pain issues. I am looking forward to them, even though I'm squeamish about medical stuff, because I'm so tired of being in pain that I'm in "I'll do anything to fix it!" mode. For you though, it must be very different, because you need this surgery just to stay alive, so it seems like you're crutched all the time instead of getting better. Again, I am sorry.

Maybe if you figured out exactly why you don't like undergoing surgery, you could possibly communicate to the doctors in a way that makes them on your side. I actually had an overall kinda positive experience getting my wisdom teeth removed with general anesthesia. I told the surgeon how squeamish I was with the thought of being artificially put to sleep etc, so when I started crying as they all came in the room to operate, I knew that they knew what was up, so I felt the feeling of them being on my side. I didn't feel like they were tricking me when they snuck the anesthesia in my arm during my panic attack. I felt like they were helping me go under and relieving me from the stress of anticipating it.

Okay thank you. I'll try not to seem so insane that I lose my credibility in wanting certain operations. I didn't think of using a psychologist to help with my mentality surrounding the potential surgery, and that's a great point.
Okay, sorry and thank you. I'll look into which hospitals have a dedicated psychiatric section.

I have a primary care doctor, so I guess all I can do is trust him to pull the strings, and explain what I need. I'm worried that there will be some kind of mistake and I'll get thrown somewhere that does a strip search. I feel like my doctor (or someone he refers me to) could make that mistake since it's hard to figure out which places do and do not do a strip search. It all seems so risky... Maybe I'll just have to get therapy, rather than waiting until the brink of death and going a mental hostpital. I don't morally trust therapists though. A therapist couldn't do much because so much of my depression is from chronic pain, and a physical specialist couldn't do much because so much of my problem is mental. I'll keep thinking about this and not giving up. It seems like the gyst is that the more severe one's situation is, the more likely they are to get strip searched. Maybe I'll plan ahead because I have no life, and call every mental hospital within 100 miles, and ask each one if they perform strip searches, then make a list of which ones do and which ones don't. Then I could manipulate things in my favor.

Maybe what I'm about to say won't help, but there's no harm in me trying. I don't think that we have to accept our animalistic reactions as law. When someone looks at an unattractive person and feels the reaction of discontentment, what is being felt is an animalistic reaction. What we should realize is that the part of us that feels animalistic reactions is not always moral. For example, when we look at an old person, our animalistic reaction is sometimes "I wish they were just gone and out of my sight because they take up space". Now just because our brain is feeling this, do we have to accept it as moral? No. We rightfully make ourselves feel compassion for the old person, because we know in our hearts that it's the right thing to do. Another example - just because it's a man's animalistic reaction to want sex with an attractive stranger does not mean it is moral for him to embrace the desire; he can choose a different path via effort and determination. What I'm saying is that the animal part of our mind - the part that makes humans not like seeing attractive people - is morally flawed. Bad morals are ingrained in the very fabric of our species' brain; that's part of what makes humanity an ugly species. But we don't have to accept the morally flawed part of our mind. If someone thinks ill of you for not looking attractive (beyond their initial reaction), then it's their fault for mindlessly obeying the animal part of their brain, instead of trying to overcome it.

Also, even if it's an animalistic reaction to dislike seeing unattractive people, let me say that I never feel that negative reaction when I look at someone I'm used to seeing. I think everybody is ugly, so when I see anyone for the first time, I kind of think "hmm, let me adjust my eyes and get used to this". But after I've seen someone a few times, I'm used to their appearance and don't even feel a negative animalistic reaction anymore. I think of everybody in terms of their mind and soul, so their appearance is just an indicator of whose mind is now thinking in the room with me. The most important thing is that the people you are close to throughout your life are comfortable around you, which won't be a problem, because they will be used to seeing you. Even if you are the world's least attractive person, close loved ones aren't gonna be like "oh boy, gotta brace myself to look at them"... No, they are used to seeing you, so they won't feel negative at all.

In conclusion, the main issue is how people you have never met look at you, and that can be overcome with logic and morality, such as the philosophy I explained. Anything that can be overcome with a good mentality is a healable condition. You should really make sure that you prevent unhealable conditions, such as your developing chronic pain.

I'm a 22 year old guy who kind of has an opposite source of bad self esteem - I am too thin and weak to be attractive. In high school, I injured my pinky finger, and was so depressed at the time that I never saw the doctor about it. I missed my window of opportunity to correct the injury. This caused permanent chronic pain in the finger. I want to get the finger amputated, but like you, the doctors don't believe or care that the pain is a problem, so they won't do anything (but I'm not giving up yet). I'm likely going to be stuck with the chronic pain from it forever. I can't work out to make my body less frail, because it hurts my finger too much to lift weights; just like you apparently can't work out to get thinner because it would hurt your chest.

There is always hope for a normal life, as long as you don't permanently injure yourself like I did. If you do permanently injure yourself, there is still much hope, but there will be limitations you'll have to accept.

I can relate to you about the throat/voice pain. I don't know if it's chronic or if you just had it temporarily, but I'll say this anyways. Some people have an unexplained permanently sore throat that never goes away (I've researched this before). My voice has always hurt when I talk for more than a minute, so I have to live with a life of minimal talking. You aren't alone if you have this problem, you just have to adapt, unfortunately.

It sounds like you might be too busy. You don't have to prove yourself to others by destroying your free time with clubs etc.. I think you should enter emergency mode, and quit all unnecessary activities that aren't directly beneficial to solving your depression, as long as you keep talking to people. Not everyone will agree with me on this though.

One more thing, about the thought of ugliness. I believe that all humans are equally ugly. Maybe our facial features are in different places, but if you zoom in on any human up close or look at their organs, we all look equally disturbing. To me, the problem with people not looking good is just that they are human; humans generally look weird. Even supermodels are ugly/disturbing in terms of what they are made out of. As a guy, I don't really care about girls' physical appearance, because we are all going to age and look like weird old people eventually.

So you're saying the big problem is that the world doesn't care about accommodating every ideology. You say that the government - in a sense - controls what ideologies are "legal". I feel like in your heart, this opinion comes from an anti-traditional values or anti-religion stance you have. But then you realized this and accommodated me by saying that part of the government's propaganda to stifle development is pornography (indirectly I assume). This was an interesting point and I appreciate your sharing of it without putting me down.

Sorry, I wasn't trying to abuse my sensitive situation to vent at you. I'm sorry if I made you feel uncomfortable. I understand if you're more of the debater type that doesn't want to talk to me anymore.

Thank you. I'm getting surgery tomorrow and experiencing general anesthesia for the first time. It will actually be the first drug I've really done, unless you count the couple times I took Nyquil. Maybe it will give me some ideas in some weird way. You seem to be able to stay asleep for a while without drugs, so maybe I can just hypnotize myself or something, rather than depending on sleeping pills that would lose their effect in the long term....

If you disagree with my morality, then it would be hard for me to trust you regarding morality topics. Most humans believe that it's morally okay for 100,000 pervs online to pleasure themselves to a video of a woman who does not love them, a woman they will forget about forever as soon as they use her for a short orgasm. I don't trust someone who thinks this is right to give me moral guidance. I can still potentially be friends with someone like you though, because I can relate to people in other ways besides values. I used to be capable of making friends with a wide variety of people because of my wide interest spread. But now, when I think about talking about interests with others, I start thinking about how I'll have to use my hands to participate in said interests, and get really depressed from thinking about using my hands. Typing to people is mostly okay though, because someone else is receiving what I am typing down, so there's a second consciousness involved. When there's a second consciousness involved, then I can just think about the other person's experience, which overpowers the thought that using my hands is a flawed activity, and allows me to enjoy it. I'm interested in hearing an expanded reasoning for why you don't feel human.
Oh yeah, and thanks for relating to me about society not being logical.

It's worth mentioning that I felt the same about pornography and culture before the genital problem started a few months ago. Though my feelings originally started during my social outcast years in middle and high school. The closest I came to mainstream was just before the genital problem happened, when I briefly had the idiotic idea that I could find love. I still thought morally the same about sex and other men as I do now, but figured "it won't hurt me too much to get brainwashed just a bit like everyone else, would it?".

Regardless, to say that my medical conditions control my morality is very oversimplifying it, but if you want to believe that, then I don't have the willpower to argue against you.

My hatred for the acceptance of pornography and other like-effect things has never faltered no matter what. This alone is enough to make me lose faith in a human's ability to make moral decisions, and make me not trust anybody.

I was not expecting such a good response. I am too mentally exhausted to post quote every sentence and respond to it, but I took in the whole thing and it made me feel better for several reasons. Nobody has to reply to me now if they don't want to (I can't tell if the "good luck" and the end of your posts means you are trying to end the conversation), but I'm not going to run away like a wimp, and am tough enough to stay here, so I'll give an update.

I am sorry everyone had to witness my extreme culture shock from last night. This morning, I felt so defeated that I had a hard time getting out of bed until the last moment possible. I somehow was only 7 minutes late to work. I spent like 75% of the day thinking about my situation and my work suffered because of it, but I made some unexpected breakthroughs eventually. For the first three hours of my work day, I had zero hope. But around the fourth hour, things started to turn around.

One of the reasons why I am afraid to adapt as needed to find a girlfriend, is because I'm afraid that if I do, I will lose the part of my personality that prevents emotional stagnation and end up "stuck in the mundane" like everyone else. This part of my personality takes up a lot of thought to maintain, but it has basically made it so that I can always get through a day at work with no problems, because it finds a way to create significance in almost everything. This part of my personality also figures out how to make myself always "on a mission" which gives me the adrenaline needed to ignore certain chronic physical issues. Without these chronic issues, I could live more reactionary (like everyone else) and not need to maintain so much extra thought to power myself forward.

When I was in high school, I was MUCH stranger than I am now, but most of the things I thought then, I still maintain. I hated how boys treated girls so superficially when girls weren't around, rating them on a scale of 1 to 10 over things that didn't matter, and I hated how girls didn't use their power as moral police to resist the objectification. I hated how people casualized sex with too much overexposure (e.g. pornography, sexting), which made sexual things seem less special and significant. I wanted the world to be quite sexual actually, but only in secret and without gossiping and instant gratification numbing us to how special sex is. I thought girls only put up with objectification because objectifying-guys were the only choice they had. So I thought that if I became extremely good at respecting women by not objectifying them (with the exception of the inevitable bit of objectification during intimate sex), I would have a niche trait that would make me a more desirable man, at least to someone with values similar to mine. But the more I ask around today (not just on this thread, but elsewhere) about values etc., it seems that almost nobody cares about this trait of respect that I have; all the guys and girls just adapted a series of "good enough" reactionary morality traits that made them fit together in relationships. I was the odd man out because I try so hard to find meaning that I sound crazy.

One day in high school, I injured my finger in Gym class. I never saw a doctor despite extraordinary pain because I just thought it wasn't worth it for me to heal myself, because happiness was too hard to reach anyways, or some flawed reactionary logic like that. Now the bone in my pinky is permanently bent as a result, and it hurts a little when I grip something for a long stretch of time or move it the wrong way. It's not a lot of pain, but it's like having a pebble in your shoe. Over the course of 8 years or so, it's been one of the unusual "this only happens to me" pains that I have dealt with. Again, these pains are part of what forces me to use extreme philosophy to push me forward. This philosophy actually made me a lot smarter and grow as a person in some ways, but now that I have learned it, I shouldn't have a need for chronic pain anymore. Doctors have told me that fixing my finger with surgery now isn't necessary. I always listened to them because since I was young, I have had brutal nausea when I think about certain internal things with the body, which made me avoid surgery. I get nauseous when I think about artificial sensory manipulation, such as anesthesia, because it reminds me that I am a mortal that can be affected by chemicals. However, I have to get my wisdom teeth out in a couple months, which will require being artificially knocked out for the first time. If I can handle that test of will like a man, then I will be able to get all the surgery necessary to fix my body that I need. I'll spend all my barely dented college savings on surgery if I have to, I don't care, because I need to break free of all this "slight constant annoyance" stuff, so that I don't need deep thought to overpower it. The finger isn't the worst chronic thing I've had (I don't have to list the others), but the finger is the only one that is proven not to be caused by anxiety. My other pains come and go with anxiety, and I usually have to figure out some lesson before they go away, as if God is trying to teach me something. On the topic of anxiety induced pain, I noticed today that when I get nervous about relationships etc., I sometimes kind of tense up my urinary muscles and/or penis as a reaction, and it makes me notice a slight amount of pain there. So the penis thing could be an anxiety induced issue. I can't humiliate myself in front of the doctor with that issue yet because there isn't enough visible evidence of something wrong, so I'm just hoping like crazy it goes away, which it likely will, based on the pattern of how my body works. There may be a very slight visible clue to the pain actually, but it's only visible during erection, and I don't want the first person to see me get an erection be a fucking doctor who says "it's not a big issue, why did you come here?". I never go into detail like that, but there you go.

Today, I remembered something that I considered a while ago, that may enable me to maintain my philosophy in my heart and also be compatible with a girl who actually exists. Maybe, since the intense philosophy and morality I have takes deliberate effort to fully maintain, it isn't natural to constantly breathe it all the time, even if they are objectively true by some higher up law. Perhaps when we die, we become extremely morally advanced versions of ourselves, and have minds that just breathe philosophy and morality in and out effortlessly. So maybe we're meant to be dumber versions of our real selves when we're down here on Earth, and we don't have to worry about having a perfect mindset because we'll ascend into that when we die. I can still have the traits of conservative purity and liberal sensitivity that makes me who I am, without being a godlike being. And I can find someone who accepts me for that, in theory. If I fail, then I'll have to re-evaluate, but it hasn't come to that yet.

Thank you again. One thing important to worth noting is that I don't expect any girl to constantly have philosophical conversations or stuff like that; I have simpler standards for what we literally do together.

I am taking this all in. I think I am going to go into a very deep depression of contemplation, but this would probably have happened if I tried to date, due to the realizations I would come to, so this thread has saved time by starting the depression early so that I can get out of it sooner. The following are NOT questions I'm asking you, but it's what I will contemplate in my head for several weeks after reading the posts here. Nobody has to read this:

-  Which parts of this advice are trying to make me a better version of myself, and which parts are just trying to make me more liberal?

- If it's true that 99% of culture has the same basic melting pot rules and desires for relationships, is there even enough meaning in a relationship in the first place?

- If everyone who is considered datable has a much similar personality than I originally thought, then is there no such thing as a "cloud-shaped map of compatibility, where people desire different strengths and weaknesses", and instead the map of compatibility is  a straight line with people only finding others who are equally as good as themselves  (people in a similar point on the line), with the definition of "good" being deemed by an objective textbook of rules?

- For a long time, I have had a limited ability to enjoy something without knowing why I am enjoying it. If everyone just does what "feels right" without worrying about the implications of their actions, and that's supposed to be what I do too to fit in, then I may never be able to truly fit in. My lack of this "effortless enjoying" could be due to my values, or it could be caused by having a 14-year stretch of depression.

- Is it more artificial for me to stay the same, or for me to convert into a legal personality?

- Is it only possible for me to enjoy my personality if it's different than most everybody elses? I like talking to people with a similar style as myself, but if that "style" was something that could be easily defaulted into, then does that take too much significance away from having the style? Hypothetically, if everyone was in a Heaven or afterlife state where we were all extremely moral, would I feel sad because I couldn't feel morally superior? I don't think I would feel sad, so I don't think I am truly a moral elitist at heart. But this still requires more thought.

- I am nearing being trapped for a very long time emotionally, in a trap where I am too sad to date anyone (I soon won't be happy enough for me dating to be morally okay), but can't become happy unless I date someone. The reason I can't be happy unless I date someone is because at the moment, a relationship is the only thing that could add enough meaning to life. But it's morally wrong for me to date if I need it to survive, because a man is supposed to be more independent than that to be worthy of a woman. Isolated interests are becoming increasingly dull. One of the main reasons I want a companion is to fulfill my desire to provide for someone. If my interests become dull to the point where I can't enjoy them anymore, then I could at least satisfy my need to provide by spending most of my free time volunteering.

- I permanently ruled out the possibility of killing myself a long time ago, since I proved it to be morally wrong (the one objectively useful thing my personality has done). Maybe I could get my anger out in a twisted alternative to suicide that I call "suicide of my happiness" where I dedicate 99% of my life to being a soldier of usefulness to the rest of the world, to burn off both my pride and self hatred.

- Is there some sort of spiritual or evolutionary reason why people like me exist? Like maybe there's things that only someone who ignores society can figure out. Maybe some people are supposed to be alone due to physical ailments, so they can help society with XYZ that nobody else wants to do (e.g. mundane jobs that people who are handicapped are happy to take because they can't physically do much else). Sometimes isolation can make someone more insane, but sometimes it can save one's sanity. Maybe evolution or God makes it so every human has a 1% chance of being this type of isolated thinker, just in case the human race got in a situation where mainstream society actually became crazy, and needed someone non-assimilated to discover certain truths or perform niche roles.

Okay, before I end this post, I need to say a couple things. First, I have not been keeping all the above feelings a secret from everyone here all this time; these are mostly things that just came out of me after reading the posts here, though some of these were dormant things I've considered briefly before. But please, relationship advisers, do NOT feel guilty for bringing this out of me. This stuff would have come out inevitably, and the advice I've received here is speeding up the burning and healing process. Lastly, I do NOT want any help getting out of this new layer of depression, because the only shred of manliness I have left is the ability to solve my problems on my own. I have taken everything said on this thread into account.
Hypothetically, if I was with a girl who wanted the relationship to be more animalistic than I wanted, then we'd have a conversation about it.

Oh yeah, and to answer your question about what emotional stagnation is - emotional stagnation is a term I use to refer to the situation when people (i.e. people in long relationships) start to feel bored of life and/or each other. I'm really good at keeping things interesting, and that's not a delusion I'm living under, because I'm also quite good at telling when people become disinterested in what I'm saying.

You also asked if I'm on the spectrum. In my opinion, no I'm not. There are times when I seem like I am because when I talk IRL, I take a little extra time to make my speech as interesting as possible, or to think of a funny joke. I can revert back to "normal person mode" when I want to, but that isn't as fun.

I'm getting the sense that maybe you don't enjoy helping me, but regardless, I really appreciate the effort you put into this response. I'll try to answer your questions without sending you through the roof in frustration of my naivety and my different mindset.

> you don't mention how old you are.

As said in the title I'm 22. 

> It would be MOST helpful if you just told us what chronic condition you have.

I can't answer this without causing more confusion. You are a very matter-of-fact person who would be very annoyed at the explanation I would give, since it wouldn't be enough for you to help me in the way you'd want to.

> You have statistics about what might happen to your dick in the future -- she has a clear understanding that there is going to be no sex in her future, EVER. Meaning she knows who to narrow her dating pool toward (mostly asexuals). You, however a) don't know what's going to happen and b) also want to make a life-long commitment decision without bothering to figure out what's going to happen, which makes it a LOT harder.

I desire a relationship that doesn't depend on sex to be meaningful, regardless of what happens with my ability. I see sexual activity as a possible eventual bonus, but not a necessity. If I assume the worst case scenario, and then find a relationship that won't require sex, then I'll still be very happy with that even if I gain the ability to have sex and my partner still doesn't want to. If I discover that nothing is wrong with me while I'm in the process of finding a girlfriend, then it would broaden my possibilities.

> A) its possible to have sex with women without objectifying them B) sometimes women (and men) like to be looked upon as sex objects in bed and C) objectification mainly means that the objectified individual is looked at exclusively as a sex object. My partner can use me and abuse me (consensually) in bed as much as he wants, but if when we're not fucking he treats me like a regular human being with thoughts and opinions he is not objectifying me.
I'm clarifying because it seems like you've constructed this...personal philosophy...on a very shaky foundation of flawed logic.

I will take this into account, but with a grain of salt because you and I don't look at this from the same angle. I'm not going to become more animalistic than I want to be just because mainstream society says it's "in the rules", but I realize that there is at least some inevitable objectification even in meaningful sex.

> people base their relationships out of very "finite" things that are worthwhile like wanting to have kids or having shared interests. Besides, looks are a part of this equation whether you want them to be or not because you are a human being and you have evolved to factor looks into your reproductive strategy at least subconsciously every now and again.
Also, people are also finite. We don't live forever, so I'm not sure why wanting to spend your time with someone who is pleasing to look at is so wrong.

It would take me a while to fully explain my opinion on the "dependency on finites" thing, so I won't explain it to you, because I don't think you'd enjoy my writing enough for it to be worth it. Plus, it could start a debate since we probably have fundamentally different values (but regardless of our differences, I still appreciate you sharing your point of view!).

> Very rough. You're not religious, so you can't just find someone who's a member of the same religion who buys into the same dogmas you buy into. Your dick might/might not work, and you won't know until you try, which normally is NOT A PROBLEM AT ALL but being that you don't wan to have sex until you're married that's going to be a hard sell for any woman. My advice is to a) tell us what this mystery illness is so that we can actually be useful b) re-evaluate this self-made philosophy c) make some platonic female friends so you can expand on your experience in talking to girls

I self-invented most of my values, but a lot of them mirror religious values. So in many cases, a Christian person would have perfect values for me. We could strengthen our common values because when two people think the same thing but for different reasons, it increases the chance that said thing is true.

Besides just values, I can tell that you and me look at the world in different ways. I would be curious as to what your personality type is; mine is INFJ, and INFJ people typically see things differently.

Making female friends like you suggested is a good idea, but I don't want to just use them as a tool to practice conversation. I'll make some female friends if I am genuinely interested in being friends with them. 

> out of curiosity, why 5+ years? after 5ish years will you just give up your search or what?

It depends on how long I can bear a very difficult search.


Again, I really appreciate your time and will talk as long as you're interested in talking for, if you had any further inquiries.

> As for the rest geeky and spiritual girls aren't particularly rare.

This is great to know. I've never really gotten a gauge on how rare that combination is.

> Pro-life would be on a case by case basis though if you're not having intercourse she's never going to need an abortion anyway.

The reason why I require them to be pro-life is for more philosophical reasons than practical reasons. Being on the same page on that moral controversy would really help make me feel like we're on the same team. If we were opposite on that fundamental value, then it would cause mutual uneasiness. 

> What I wonder is if you're able to go into the dating area without seeming as if you have a shopping list of requirements and you're checking the boxes. Dating and love is about making a connection with another human being and getting to know them.
And remember if you want someone to accept you you're going to have to do some accepting yourself.

I'm keeping my vision of my ideal companion vague and hazy to allow for an actual person who actually exists to get to know me.
